clue.text: Some went wrong, not finishing garden feature

parts.note: some of a thing is a part of it

indicators.note: the word is cut short before its final letter, so it does not reach its finish

parts.note: to have gone wrong is to have erred

explanation.surface: A gardener's plans went awry and a feature was left half-built.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not finishing' drops the last letter of ERRED, leaving ERRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A parterre is a formal ornamental garden of patterned flower beds, a classic feature of grand gardens.

clue.text: Pulveriser of nasty insect left on back of house

parts.note: a pest is a troublesome insect

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, here taken from house

explanation.surface: A dangerous bug has been left crawling on the rear wall of a house.
explanation.definitionFit: The club-shaped tool pounds substances to powder in a mortar, so it is literally a grinder.

clue.text: Tailor played Venetian bridge

indicators.note: the letters are played with, rearranged as a musician might improvise on a tune

explanation.surface: A tailor performed music on a famous bridge in Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rialto is the oldest and best-known bridge over Venice's Grand Canal.

clue.text: People on their own before having little ones

parts.note: ere is a poetic word for before
mites are tiny creatures, or affectionately small children

explanation.surface: Solitary people found themselves with small children before long.
explanation.definitionFit: Eremites are hermits, religious recluses who live in solitude.

clue.text: Attack sees king needing help

parts.note: R, from the Latin rex, is the usual abbreviation for king
aid means help

explanation.surface: A monarch under assault calls for assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: A raid is a sudden assault or incursion.

clue.text: Rich person collects minimal cash for confidential info

indicators.note: the rich man's word gathers the other piece up inside itself

parts.note: a toff is a British slang word for a wealthy upper-class person
one penny, written 1P, is the smallest sum, read here as the letters IP

explanation.surface: A wealthy man pockets a tiny sum in exchange for passing on a secret.
explanation.walkthrough: The figure 1 in 1P (one penny, the smallest British coin) is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A tip-off is a private warning or piece of inside information.

clue.text: One refusal to accept small child entirely

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: the refusal word takes in, or accepts, the child word inside it

parts.note: no is a refusal
a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: Someone flatly refuses to take in a little child at all.
explanation.definitionFit: In toto is Latin for completely or as a whole.

clue.text: Completely drunk thug involved with riot

indicators.note: the letters stagger about like a drunk and land in a new order

explanation.surface: A completely intoxicated thug got caught up in a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges THUG with RIOT; 'involved with' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Outright means wholly or without reservation, as in 'won outright'.

clue.text: Searching for a drink before start of gala

parts.note: gin is an alcoholic drink

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, here taken from gala

explanation.surface: Someone looks for a drink before a celebration gets going.
explanation.definitionFit: Foraging is hunting around for food or supplies, a kind of searching.

clue.text: Eve's bit of pork

parts.note: Genesis tells that Eve was made from one of Adam's ribs, an extra one he could do without, and the same words name a cut of pork

explanation.definitionFit: A spare rib is a cut of pork ribs, and in the Bible story Eve was created from Adam's rib.

clue.text: Old coin found in country river

parts.note: a state is a nation or country

explanation.surface: An ancient coin was discovered in a river somewhere abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: The stater was a gold or silver coin of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Generous policeman promises to pay

parts.note: cop is slang for a police officer
an IOU, 'I owe you', is a written promise to pay; IOUS is the plural

explanation.surface: A big-hearted police officer hands out written pledges of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Copious means abundant or plentiful, generous in quantity.

clue.text: Little Charlotte's fate, a situation in which no one wins

parts.note: one's lot is one's fate or destiny

parts.words: a situation in which no one wins
parts.note: a tie is a draw, where neither side wins

explanation.surface: A young girl's destiny is a stalemate.
explanation.definitionFit: Lottie is a familiar pet-name form of Charlotte.

clue.text: Value home on front of good seaside resort

parts.note: worth means value
to be in is to be at home

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter, here taken from good

explanation.surface: A house on a good seafront is worth a lot.
explanation.walkthrough: WORTHING is a seaside town on the south coast of England, in West Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: Worthing is an English coastal town popular with holidaymakers.

clue.text: Chap Douglas provides home for?

parts.note: Douglas is not a man's name here but the capital of the Isle of Man, so the chap is a native of that island

explanation.surface: A question about where a fellow called Douglas lives.
explanation.walkthrough: Douglas wants to be a person's first name; it is the capital town of the Isle of Man, a self-governing island in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A Manxman is a man from the Isle of Man, whose capital is Douglas.

clue.text: A live TV broadcast in foreign city

indicators.note: broadcast also means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A television programme is shown live from a city abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Tel Aviv is a major city in Israel, foreign from the British setter's viewpoint.

clue.text: Recoil from second invader crossing north sea

parts.note: Hun was British slang for the German forces of the World Wars, who raided Britain across the North Sea

explanation.surface: People draw back from an attacker coming over from the far side of the North Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: To shun is to avoid or shrink away from someone or something.

clue.text: Repeated strange rite on new date

indicators.note: strange signals that the letters of rite are made odd, put in a fresh order
new signals that the letters of date are given a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An odd ceremony is performed again on a fresh date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' turns RITE into ITER and 'new' turns DATE into ATED.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to say or do again, so iterated means done over again.

clue.text: Inform charmingly old-fashioned bill first

indicators.note: first says the bill's letters go at the front, ahead of the other piece

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill
quaint means attractively old-fashioned

explanation.surface: A notice tells you the quaint old invoice must be paid before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquaint someone with something is to make them familiar with it, to tell them.

clue.text: Be a moment getting together with girl

parts.note: a trice is an instant, as in 'in a trice'

explanation.surface: Someone stops for a moment to meet up with a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Beatrice is a girl's name.

clue.text: Mexican dish old moggy knocked over

indicators.note: knocking something over turns it upside down, so the run of letters is turned back to front

parts.note: moggy is British slang for an ordinary cat

explanation.surface: An elderly cat upset a plate of Mexican food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked over' reverses OCAT. A moggy is everyday British slang for a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A taco is a Mexican folded tortilla with a filling.

clue.text: Old flame swore: 'not right, being let off!'

parts.note: an ex is a former partner, an old flame

indicators.note: not signals that the right letter is removed from the swearing word

parts.note: cursed means swore

explanation.surface: A former lover cursed when let off the hook unfairly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not right' removes R from CURSED, leaving CUSED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be excused is to be released from a duty or punishment.

clue.text: It's like spring too

parts.note: as means like, as in 'dressed as a clown'
a well is a spring of water

explanation.surface: It resembles a spring as well.
explanation.definitionFit: As well means also or in addition.

clue.text: Headgear good for Parisian having open fabric

parts.note: bon is French for good
net is an open-mesh fabric

explanation.surface: A Paris hat-maker thinks a hat made of mesh is good.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonnet is a hat tied under the chin.

clue.text: Artist turning up for a prize

indicators.note: in a down entry turning up means reading the word from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a drawer is someone who draws, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter appears to collect an award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses DRAWER in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A reward is something given in recognition, a prize.

clue.text: Philosopher has things for the bride heading off

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, which is taken off

parts.note: a trousseau is the clothes and linen a bride gathers for her marriage

explanation.surface: A thinker owns the wedding things a bride takes away with her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' removes the first letter T from TROUSSEAU.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Jacques Rousseau was an eighteenth-century Genevan philosopher.

clue.text: Pet runs into Midlands town

indicators.note: into shows the runs letter going inside the town name

parts.note: Stoke-on-Trent, often called Stoke, is a town in the English Midlands
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An animal dashes into a town in central England.
explanation.walkthrough: STOKE (Stoke-on-Trent) is a pottery town in the Midlands of England.
explanation.definitionFit: To pet an animal is to stroke it fondly.

clue.text: Confront alternate notes on treble stave

explanation.definitionFit: To face is to confront; the four spaces of the treble stave, read upward, are the notes F, A, C, E, which lie between the line notes.

clue.text: Worked hard? It's time to get lubricated!

parts.note: oiled means lubricated

explanation.surface: After hard work it is time for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lubricated' wants to mean drunk in the surface; here it is simply greased.
explanation.definitionFit: To toil is to labour hard, so toiled means laboured.

clue.text: Echidna wrecked a large estate

indicators.note: something wrecked is broken up, so the letters are smashed and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A spiny anteater wrecked a big ranch.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacienda is a large ranch or plantation in Spanish-speaking countries.

clue.text: Churchwarden's bit left over?

parts.note: a churchwarden is also a long clay tobacco pipe, and the bit left over is the half-burnt plug of tobacco at the bottom of the bowl

explanation.surface: A church official is left with a scrap after the service.
explanation.walkthrough: A churchwarden here is not a parish officer but a long-stemmed clay pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Dottle is the plug of unsmoked tobacco left in a pipe after smoking.

clue.text: Hated exam — action taken to circumvent it

indicators.note: to circumvent is to go around, so the action word goes around the exam word

parts.note: a deed is an action
a test is an exam

explanation.surface: A student loathed an exam and took steps to dodge it.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest is to loathe intensely, so detested means loathed.
